solution: \(f'(x) = 2x^{2} - x - (2x - 1)\sin x = (2x - 1)(x - \sin x)\). The factor \(x - \sin x\) has the same sign as \(x\). For \(x \geq \frac{1}{2}\) both factors are non-negative, so \(f'(x) \geq 0\) and \(f\) increases in \(\left[\frac{1}{2}, \infty\right)\), which is option A. For \(0 < x < \frac{1}{2}\), \(f'(x) < 0\); but for \(x < 0\) both factors are negative, so \(f'(x) > 0\) and \(f\) does not decrease on all of \(\left(-\infty, \frac{1}{2}\right]\). That rules out B, and C and D fail by the same signs.
note: said f'(x) <= 0 on all of (-inf, 1/2]; for x < 0 both factors are negative so f' > 0. Sign analysis corrected; key A unchanged.
